audit.summary: Three Major proof problems are established: an invalid nonsymmetric matrix inference in Lemma 2.17, a false scaled-coordinate reduction equivalence in Theorem 6.6, and a circular connectedness argument in Lemma 2.29. A separate Minor quantifier defect in Lemma 2.28 has an exact admissible saddle witness. No main-theorem falsity is claimed.
limitations: P1 — Positive eigenvalues do not imply positive quadratic forms — Counterevidence: Lemma 2.17 itself is not disproved. In the two-variable unit-weight case, ordered coordinates are recoverable from their first two moments.
P2 — The reduction map omits the factors 2 and 6 — Counterevidence: The adjacent text consistently uses (2e2,6e3), strongly indicating a local omitted scaling. No undecidability theorem is refuted.

P3 — Lemma 2.28 includes saddle critical points outside its stated types — Counterevidence: This saddle is not a boundary-extremum counterexample. Restricting the assertion to local extrema is the natural repair direction; the printed Vtilde index also needs reconciliation.

P4 — The connectedness proof ends with its own starting assumption — Counterevidence: No counterexample to the Vandermonde connectedness statement is asserted. A generic disconnected compact union of two line segments with singleton nonempty slices only illustrates why the supplied slice argument is logically insufficient.
Limitations: Complete page reading is not a complete independent verification of every proof.
Limitations: No claims that main geometry or undecidability theorems are false; three Major findings concern invalid or incomplete central derivations.
Limitations: Minor P3 disproves only an overbroad all-critical-points assertion; its saddle does not refute the intended boundary-extremum classification.

proposition.claim:
The finite probability simplex is \(\Delta_{n-1}=\{x\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^n:\sum_i x_i=1\}\). The paper studies the images of power sums \(p_j(x)=\sum_i x_i^j\), including generalized increasing integer exponents. In the ordered chamber, a multiplicity vector \((m_0,m_1,\ldots,m_\ell)\) records zero coordinates followed by increasing distinct positive coordinates. Type (1) requires \(m_{2i-1}=1\), while type (2) requires \(m_0=0\) and \(m_{2i}=1\). The sub-probability simplex replaces the equality by \(\sum_i x_i\leq1\). Squaring variables converts these domains to a sphere or ball and doubles the exponents. That transformation is useful, but it can introduce degenerate objective directions at zero coordinates, as Problem 3 demonstrates.

The elementary-symmetric convex-hull result in Section 5 has a direct supporting argument. For a linear combination of elementary symmetric polynomials, fixing all but two positive coordinates and their sum leaves an expression \(C x_1x_2+D\). A minimizer with maximal zero support either permits another zero coordinate when \(C\geq0\), or forces the two positive coordinates equal when \(C<0\). Thus some minimizer is uniform on its nonzero support. Applying this to every affine functional, and using separation, gives the claimed convex hull of these uniform-support images. This support-function argument also avoids any need to assume that every extreme point of an arbitrary compact convex set is uniquely exposed. The triangular polynomial change from \((t,\ldots,t^{d-1})\) to \[\left(\frac{(1-t)}{2!},\frac{(1-t)(1-2t)}{3!},
 \ldots,\frac{\prod_{j=1}^{d-1}(1-jt)}{d!}\right)\] has nonzero leading coefficients. It verifies the invertible affine correspondence used for the cyclic-polytope vertices. The hook-shaped test in Theorem 5.8 then follows from homogeneity and linearity on \(e_1=1\).

Recorded check: All entries and determinant 2 are positive; eigenvalues (7±sqrt(41))/2 are distinct positive, but v^T A v=-1/4 and the orthogonal compression to span(v)=-1/29. A is the actual Jacobian of (x1+x2,x1^2+x2^2) at (2,3).

repair.content:
Replace the inference with a valid injectivity/univalence argument for the ordered weighted power-sum map and verify boundary-face regularity under the full exponent/weight hypotheses.

Use 2e2/e1^2 and 6e3/e1^3 in every group in tau. Homogenizing power 3 deg(f) still clears denominators.

State precisely the relevant extrema and justify the zero-coordinate cases; smooth constraint surfaces do not remove the degenerate zero-coordinate directions.

Supply an independent proof that the attainable p1-range is an interval (or another valid connectedness argument), covering singular values; combine compactness and connected fibers correctly. Merely replacing the final word is insufficient.
